transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because for a long time now, my sleep has just been... broken. I mean, I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And after all that, I end up awake before my alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you become worried or tense about your sleep when you are trying to fall asleep?

No, not really. I mean, I don't lie there stressing about whether I'll sleep or not. I'm usually so tired from my shifts that I just kind of crash right away. It's more about what happens after I fall asleep, so... no, I wouldn't say I get worried or tense about actually falling asleep.
How long has this broken sleep been happening?
Well, it's been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us. That was... a little over two years ago now.
How does your broken sleep affect you during the day?

Well, it just leaves me feeling completely drained. By the time I finish seeing my home-health clients and come back to help out at the house... my body just feels so heavy. It's like I have nothing left in the tank. Even just doing the basic things, like charting my work notes or folding some laundry, it can feel like it's just too much to push through.
When you wake during the night, do you have a quiet, comfortable place and enough time available to sleep?

Yeah, I do. Our bedroom is comfortable, and it's pretty quiet at night once everyone is finally settled. And I definitely have enough time... I make sure to get in bed early enough before my morning shifts. So, yeah, the room and the schedule are fine. I just... I just can't seem to stay asleep.
On average, how many nights per week do you wake up and have trouble staying asleep?
I'm not really sure on an exact number, to be honest. I haven't kept track of it that closely... it just feels like it happens a lot, but I couldn't tell you exactly how many nights a week it is.
In a typical week, on how many nights do you wake up and have trouble getting back to sleep?
Like I said, I really don't know the exact number. I haven't been counting. It's just... it happens enough that I'm always tired, but I couldn't give you a specific amount of days per week.
If you had to estimate, on how many nights in a typical week does this happen?
I honestly couldn't even give you a good guess. The nights just kind of blur together at this point. I'm sorry, I really just don't have a specific number for you.
Has anyone noticed you snoring loudly or gasping or choking during sleep?
No, not that I know of. No one has ever mentioned anything like that to me, so I don't think I snore or gasp in my sleep.
Would you say this difficulty staying asleep happens at least three nights in a typical week?

Yeah, I'd say it's at least three nights. It's just... for a long time now, my sleep has been completely broken. I fall into bed exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm up before the alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all.
